title: Heritage designation dropped for Weber Street East co-op
subtitle: Queen Street North heritage permit deferred to January; Belmont Village snow removal, 2027 calendar, and write-offs approved.
overview: Council decided not to proceed with a heritage designation for 265 Weber Street East, a 15-unit housing co-op, after its volunteer board objected. Council accepted the objection {{vote:m1}}, and the related designation by-law was removed from the agenda. Under the legislation the property will come off the City's heritage register at year end and cannot be re-listed for five years.

Council also deferred a heritage permit for 16-20 Queen Street North to a January 2027 meeting {{vote:m2}}, so the owner can keep discussing community benefit space and the changes with staff and the neighbourhood. It approved a new snow removal service for part of the Belmont Village BIA {{vote:m9}}, the 2027 meeting calendar {{vote:m12}}, and write-offs of uncollectable accounts. It also approved a notice of intention to designate 105-117 Onward Avenue {{vote:m7}}.

Compass Kitchener reported that all twelve strategic plan projects it reviewed met or exceeded expectations. The Mayor announced a plan to support local businesses and protect jobs amid tariff uncertainty, and Council recognized long-serving volunteer groups.

decisions.detail: Council accepted the co-op's objection, directed staff to take no further action on the proposed Part IV heritage designation, and directed the Clerk to publish a notice of withdrawal {{vote:m1}}.

Council deferred the heritage permit application, which covers part of the side return and a second-floor window-to-door alteration, to a January 2027 meeting to allow further discussion between the applicant, staff and the neighbourhood.

Council approved a heritage permit to demolish a single detached dwelling and build a new one, on condition of a tree management plan and arborist report and heritage clearance of final building permit drawings.
Council directed the Clerk to publish a notice of intention to designate 105-117 Onward Avenue under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act.
Council approved Option 3 as a new special snow removal service for part of the Belmont Village BIA, with the levy rate to be set through the annual budget.
Council wrote off $59,839 in uncollectable miscellaneous receivable accounts against the allowance for doubtful receivables.
Council wrote off $310,571 in uncollectable utility accounts against the allowance for doubtful utility receivables.
Council approved the 2027 Council and Committee calendar, delegated authority to schedule extra planning committee meetings on Council dates where needed, and allowed rescheduling by resolution.

debate: Delegates for the Weber Street East co-op said the evidence did not clearly support at least two heritage criteria, pointing to similar nearby buildings and replaced windows, railings and other features. They also said the co-op is run by a small group of volunteers and its reserve fund is limited.

Staff said designation does not require physical changes, that the windows are not identified as heritage attributes, and that changes to listed features would need a heritage permit, with flexibility on materials. Staff considered six of nine criteria met and doubted a deferral would change the outcome. They said the item was before Council because of the deadline for reviewing heritage register properties.

Councillors who supported withdrawing the notice cited affordability for co-op residents, the care already given to the building, and the potential cost of a heritage impact assessment. One councillor raised whether the decision sets a precedent for other co-ops. Others noted that the co-op is not-for-profit and compared it with a downtown building that was not designated.

On 16-20 Queen Street North, the applicant's planner asked for a deferral because questions about the ground-floor community benefit space were unresolved. Other delegates supported more time and said affordable housing, cultural space and heritage should be considered together given the changed project. A councillor also asked for a missing engineer's report on the facade.
Staff noted that a deferral to the next council's first round of meetings in January was the realistic option, since only one more meeting of this council and one round in December remained.
